title: I am paying for prime delivery…
content:
I am paying for Prime delivery, but Amazon Flex drivers are becoming increasingly inconsistent and inefficient. What is the point of paying for Prime with overnight delivery if multiple Amazon Flex drivers do not deliver within the originally promised timeframe? Maybe it’s just my town that has an Amazon Flex driver issue, but I have had multiple packages either not delivered at all or consistently late.

What I have been doing to get around this is placing another overnight order for the same items to get a better delivery driver, and then returning the original items after that. Usually, this allows me to get my items in a timely fashion. I still get my money back, and I get my items when promised.

It’s actually kind of funny that I can even do this to get my items on time. It really goes to show the lack of consistency with delivery drivers in my town, and a deeper problem with Amazon gig work system.

Also, Amazon wants customers to use manufacturer packaging to be eco-friendly, but in the very same breath, Amazon will have multiple packages delivered to the same house by multiple cars in one day. That is a pretty huge contradiction. That’s the exact opposite of eco-friendly.

Edit: I guess I should be grateful Amazon even manages to deliver 1 out of 2 packages instead of none. The bar is super low at this point. If this company was actually eco-friendly they would have both packages delivered by one person instead of shipping them separately. That way 2 of 2 packages have a chance of being delivered instead of 1 of 2.

content:
Put Explore, Shop By Interest, & Your likes on the person page, where customers access their account, profile, shopping activities, settings, etc.

True shopping is an event with friends, or family. Taking all day, getting lunch, & having a good time. AI will delete that from the Amazon the shopping experience. Allowing the shopper to arrive for a certain purchase & look around for other things as they want, is key. AI directing the path is not shopping. Using AI for information, app/website troubles, product details, & as a servant that serves the customer rather than what steers the person is a better approach.

title: Search ignores my terms; filters and sponsored listings make it worse
content:
Search terms are frequently ignored. Products with no clear connection to what I typed show up mixed into results, forcing me to manually weed out irrelevant items that a basic keyword match should have excluded.

Manual filters don't work reliably. When I apply filters (price, rating, etc.), products that clearly meet those criteria are sometimes excluded anyway — filters should narrow results, not produce inconsistent ones.

Sponsored listings crowd out real results. The volume of sponsored placements — often unrelated to my search — pushes down genuinely relevant products and makes it harder to compare and choose.

Net effect: shopping now requires extra effort to undo Amazon's assumptions about what I want, instead of just searching and browsing freely.

title: Amazon has removed this app’s functionality for devices in Lockdown Mode, same for their website.
content:
The Good: the app used to work, without customer service support, across tablet and phone, that were in Lockdown Mode. Affording easy purchase options to its customers.

The Bad: who gets the blame and who needs more user data? The app has worked, minus any customer service functionalities, without much issue while this device has been in Lockdown Mode for years. Suddenly over the past couple weeks product images no longer populated with some other weird actions like changing the quantity of an item in your shopping cart made the product images visible. Leave the app and come back and those images are gone again.

There are some logical reasons why apps become useless when a device is in Lockdown Mode: data collection, poor app development (Apple iPadOS security updates, Amazon app). This device OS has not been updated in 18-months making it highly unlikely to be Apple’s the OS. Meanwhile the Amazon app was updated last week if not mistaken. This reeks of data-collection and truly how much more is needed from Amazon’s customers.

It is great when device manufacturers allow users to turn on extended security only in as much as the app developers know and do build a functional app with these active security restrictions.

Again, security and user protections are pointless if the convenience of a mobile device is forfeited. Suggest using a web browser on a non-Lockdown Mode device; 4 separate browsers returned no data when attempting to visit Amazon.com.

Amazon has intentionally hamstrung their iOS/iPadOS app and the Amazon website for devices in Lockdown Mode. Their argument will be “security” or “fraud” or anything other than honesty.

Turning off Lockdown Mode restores all functionality across the app and the browsers.

Shameful.

title: Disappointed.
content:
I have loved Amazon for centuries, but now, I am so disappointed at how awful the delivery process has become.
Amazon once had their own Prime delivery service, a very reliable top-notch delivery system with trained drivers and strong logistics. Now, they have out-sourced to third-party companies that have horrible oversight and poor training for those undertaking the delivery. Drivers call me on my personal phone number, confused and clearly unable to use the GPS affectively. Often to the point to where they do not even know the address of where they are going. Clearly, on the package as well as GPS system operations provided by the service is the address which the driver can simply enter into a GPS. It is 2026. Before smart phones there was even a TomTom GPS that did this.
The quality of delivery has crossed the line to privacy breach as the drivers call my personal phone number harrassingly demanding me to give them a complete walk-through on how to get here. Ridiculous. Unnecessary. Not following the directions of their GPS is not my responibility for them.
So, they call me again and again after I ask them to STOP calling me, which is now a breach of privacy.
I should not, at any moment of the day, be responsible for the delivery based on whether I am available to pick up a call on my personal phone number.
Unfortunately, it has come to such an awful consenses that these delivery companies DEMAND your personal phone number in order to do the delivery. They will call you and text you continuously screaming. Phone calls, voice messages and texts.
Even, I have had multiple drivers ASK FOR MY LIVE LOCATION!
These are very concerning security breaches. Absolutely unsafe and invades vital privacy.

I know only use this app for items that I can’t find anywhere else. I no longer buy anything that costs more than $50 because of the deceitful practices.

I caution you to be careful with purchases. Beware of their deceitful marketing and item(s) descriptions. More importantly, read the reviews on the app on Trustpilot, Google, and on Reddit before purchasing.

title: Amazing Shopping, beautiful interface, but could use improvement
content:
No subscriptions that limit access to purchasable content, no fees for using the app (Besides shipping fees), easy access to app tools, great search engine. The only problem I have noticed was that certain items would not show up when searched for, likely due to low popularity. Then again, there are search filters for this very reason. I just wish I could find a product by inputting a brief description of it along with its brand. Maybe we could try implementing an AI search assistant similar to the one used in product analysis.
One feature I would like to see in the future is the option to enable some sort of low-light dark mode through settings or some sidebar and/or pop-up message.
I would highly recommend this app to anyone, since it doesn’t take up a lot of storage, there are a lot of features, and new products coming in on a daily basis. You can even get your homepage to be customized with products you may be interested in! I find this app very helpful, even if you aren’t comfortable with purchasing anything directly from the app. Hope this review helps out those who read it.

title: AI support and lack of ability to report bugs ruins an otherwise functional app
content: The constant rerouting to AI support is the downfall of Amazon’s iOS app. There is no way to give user feedback, and often no way to speak with a human except through multiple rounds of automated rerouting. This is incredibly frustrating when you are repeatedly routed through the same questions multiple times. This is a new issue within the past year, and although some experiences are better, when you wish to report an issue that does not fit in a neat box of predetermined problems, the experience is universally poor. The human agents you do speak to also seem less with the program than in the past. I have to wonder how simple bugs are identified when no one on the user end can even report them without a lengthy customer service experience they are surely uninterested in. For example: There is currently a bug that prevents certain grocery item substitution rejections from being processed in app, leading to poor substitutions. But is there any way for me to report this or even give feedback on this? Absolutely not. I can request a refund, but I cannot give any context or flag the bug.

I’ve had one box of books come in previously where the paper was stuffed between the books & on top. They arrived in perfect condition. I’d love to be able to have the option to request that & im willing to pay a small fee for that extra effort and material.

title: Just be honest
content:
I needed computer parts for a build I’m helping a friend with, and I saw that they would arrive on the last day of his trip. I figured I’d take the chance, thinking if they didn’t show up, I could always run to a store earlier in the day and just pay more and cancel the order. I checked the app when the driver was just one stop away, and I was relieved. But then we got distracted with other things (the parts were small and inexpensive, so we left them at the door, or so we thought). Around 10 p.m., I went to check for the package as we where to the point of needing them—and there was nothing. I checked the app, and it still said “out for delivery.” I contacted customer service, and after speaking with an associate, I was told it would definitely arrive tonight.

Now, I check again, and suddenly it’s delayed due to weather and “being processed” at the facility. The worst part? The driver had already passed my house, and I literally watched him drive back down the street, thinking he had already stoped by. At that point, it wasn’t just an issue—it was a complete lack of care and professionalism. This experience, from the misleading updates to the lack of follow-through, deserves nothing less than a 1-star review. There was zero reason my package couldn’t have been dropped off when the driver was in front of my house… just be honest.

Also, if you’re in your cart and paused scrolling on an item, and then you leave the screen, it would be great if it takes you back to where you left off. This is a shopping app so the general idea of leaving things where you left off is very helpful.

author: Bella Weis

title: Don’t pay extra for fast shipping, not worth it.
content:
I paid extra for shipping to get a package delivered as fast as possible, not wanting to commit to prime. This is my first time doing so and I’m never doing it again. It said it will be 1-2 days, which was good enough for me, I had a reason as to why I needed within the next 1 or two days. The other option was free shipping to get it with in 5 days. Anyways, my package was out for delivery, only 8 stops away, which was not bad. Suddenly the app lost connection to the truck, never restored the signal to the truck back. Now it said it will be delivered by 10 pm. It hit that time, then it said it would still be delivered today. 30 minutes pass, it now says I won’t get it within the 5 day range. So i basically paid extra for no reason. Now I’m worried because I’m not sure if they lost my package? Or maybe delivered it to the wrong house?. Or for some reason they returned it to the ware house last minute?. Not sure, but is safe to say I’m never doing it again. Oh! And the kicker is! It won’t let me track my package at all to see what happened to it, or it won’t let me refund it after those days.

Regardless of all of that, I haven’t had any issues with the app. Just that.

author: Potato_Bug

title: Absolutely atrocious recently
content:
I have enjoyed this app, and it is absolutely amazing, obviously for what it allows us to do at its core. It completes its biggest purpose which is allowing you to shop, add things to your cart, and pay for items.
However, on the tech side of things, there is a number of serious issues recently that seems to be unaddressed. For example, when you touch reviews, it loads a bunch of recommended products, and actually does not take you to the review section. You have to scroll all the way to the top of the page and then touch the reviews again to now go to the reviews, because of all of the recommended products that were loaded directly into your point of view. Very poor design choice.

Another major issue seems to be that for a majority of product pages, you will be taken to an error screen, and the page will refuse to load.

One more thing I will mention I have noticed as a glitch, is that when using airplay, anytime you encounter an ad that has a video component to it, it will forcefully play on whatever airplay device you were using at the moment. It will not ask your permission, it will just immediately take over on that device.

I definitely need these simple things fixed before I can reinstate my five star score.

content: I know that no one is going to read this or care, but I have to say it anyway. In a recent update they changed the UI on the iPad. Really I think they just got too lazy to maintain a separate iPad version, and I hate that more and more companies are doing this with their iPad version apps.

title: Unusable after recent update
content:
I have been a long-time user of this app and always appreciated its functionality and ease of use. However, after the most recent update, it has become completely unusable on IPhone IOS 18. What was once a seamless experience has now turned into constant frustration.

Here are the key issues since the update:
- Frequent Crashes: The app crashes within minutes of opening, making it impossible to complete even the simplest tasks.
- Slow Performance: The app is painfully slow. Features that used to load instantly now take an eternity, if they load at all.
- Unresponsive Interface: Buttons and menus often don’t respond to taps or clicks. I find myself tapping multiple times just to get a reaction, and even then, it’s a 50/50 chance the app will process the input.
- Loss of Key Features: Some of the app’s most useful features have either been removed or hidden behind complicated menus, making it harder to navigate and use.
- Bugs and Glitches: I’ve encountered numerous bugs, from text disappearing to images not loading properly. It feels like the app was released without proper testing.

title: Poor accessibility features
content: Being vision impaired, online shopping is vital for me as it is very frustrating and time consuming to shop in store when you can’t tell what items are or look at labels. Accessibility features are also a vital part of shopping, as well. This app does not have a dark mode and does not work with the accessibility features on my phone, so text is way too small for me to read. I’ve turned on smart invert so that I can at least see what’s on the screen if I use my magnifier, but because this app doesn’t work with the features on my phone, pictures get inverted, too, so I can’t look at the product unless I go turn the invert off for a sec and then turn it back on so I can order something. It’s annoying and makes it more difficult for me to find what I need, so I’ll often just shop somewhere else that does have dark mode and larger/bolder text options. They’d get more money out of me if they added these features

title: Search autocomplete doesn’t work anymore
content:
When searching for an item on the app, usually suggestions will appear below the search bar so that you don’t have to type out the full name of the product you’re searching for. The suggestions will usually have a little arrow on the right that you used to be able to click to have that suggestion autocomplete in the search bar. However, now whenever you click the arrow in a suggested search result, nothing happens. You have the actually click on the search result itself which prompts the app to begin searching for that result, and then click on the search bar again to edit or modify the search query.

Basically, you now need to type out the full name of the product even if similar product appear in the search suggestions. The search suggestions are now useless because you can no longer click the arrow to autocomplete and then edit the autocompleted suggestion to your specific search query.

author: Mia.11

title: Very good app, but a few improvements would go a long way
content:
As someone who uses this app almost daily, even if I don’t plan on making another purchase until a week or a month from that day, I find it a great way to keep track of things I’m considering, options I’d like to keep in mind, and method of keeping all of my “thoughts” in one place: that place is the seemingly never-ending list which is better known as the items I’ve saved for later.

And, this leads to what is one of two primary ways in which I believe this app could be improved, and that is to make it easier, more intuitive, and faster to create shopping lists of “liked” items. The lists feature as it currently exists is great — if you already know what you’d like to add to it. But, if you’re like me and enjoy browsing in order to discover what you’d like to add, it is not necessarily easy to navigate into the lists of favorited items, nor is it always easy for me — as someone who relies on enlarging the screen as I navigate because of vision loss — to even find the little heart icon which must be clicked to add a item to a list.

The other improvement I would love would be an overhaul of the search engine: it is frustrating to know I’m missing potentially hundreds of items because they are not all easily found by the current search engine function, where typing in “dress red” and “red dress” may very well yield two totally different sets of results in a seemingly chaotically random order, even when attempting to sort those results into any sort of desired order. The filters are often highly inaccurate, and many results left out of what is found — either due to lack of proper indexing or possibly due to originally being indexed in another format, language, app or program.

Overall, it’s a fabulous app, but there’s room for improvement that would go a very long way to making it absolutely perfect.

title: Feature Request
content:
Few ideas:
1) I love that I can track purchases to I do. However, someone else is sending something to my home and I have no access to tracking that incoming package to my home. Please create a feature that lists packages coming to my address from someone else’s account. Thanks in advance!

In addition, there isn’t a filter for prioritizing Organic and Non-GMO product which causes many more hours and system hits looking for the Organic/Non-GMO requests.   Please add a filter to allow the user to prioritize Organic/Non-GMO product preferences.

Thank you all!!   I hope to see these improvements in the future.

Thank you!!

Do better next time.

author: tinifairy

title: Decent, but filters need more work.
content:
The app is well-designed and easy to use, but when browsing clothes, the filters just don’t work most of the time.

If you want something long sleeve, you put the long sleeve filter on, and you’d expect long sleeve products to show up, but you end up with sleeveless or short sleeve.

Testing this out for dresses too ends up with even worse results, with the fabric type filter just not working most of the time. Let’s say you want something made of cotton, so you use the cotton fabric type filter, and results will range from actually being cotton to having absolutely no relevance to cotton.

Additionally, some of the products that actually do fulfill the requirements for the filter actually get filtered out and don’t appear after the filter is applied, thus making the filter pretty useless, for example, we’ll say that you are looking for a dress solid in color, with long bell sleeves. Applying that filter will end up with some with that requirement, but most of the others having short sleeves, patterns, and regular short sleeves.

Applying the filter and sorting from cheapest also just doesn’t yield good results, where you can end up with that products that have nothing to do with the search in the top result. Let’s say you’re looking for shirts but you get microphones instead. It’s really bizarre.

Filters are supposed to help you narrow down a search out of tens of thousands of products, not hinder them.

title: It works well until it doesn’t.
content:
The process of communicating with sellers is hard to access.

Also be wary of who those sellers are!

I had a very expensive battery shipped to me via FedEx ground that never showed up at my door. FedEx marked it as delivered and someone else signed for it. Unsurprisingly, after making a missing package claim with them the claim was closed and no explanation was given as to what happened there.

The process of getting a refund for this has been painstaking to say the very least. Who knows if it will even work.

After fumbling through the app I finally figured out how to contact the seller which happens to be a Chinese company. No way to call them or email them- just communicate through the app.

The correspondence with them has been awful. Repeated messages that are poorly written from multiple “people”. Even when I clearly tell them that a claim needs to be made with FedEx and I give clear instructions on how to remedy the situation they send back some B.S.

So a word of caution- be wary of the cogs in this machine, or you may end up like me… almost 2k in the hole and doing all of the legwork to try and make things right.

I will spend my hard earned money with smaller businesses that actually appreciate me and follow through with their commitments.

title: New UI is bloated and broken
content:
The new UI is terrible. Instead of tidy text menus I have to scroll through a whole page of visual lists with horizontally scrolling images . It takes so long to find anything now. It’s overwhelming and uses so much space that often the thing I’m looking for is beyond the bottom of the screen. Having a fixed menu on the bottom is just bad design. Less vertical space and not where people look for a menu.

It also rotates to portrait orientation on every screen change. How did QA miss that?  This app is nearly unusable on iPad now. If it’s the same bloated UI on the phone I feel sorry for phone users having to scroll endlessly to find what they’re looking for. The UX team needs to do more research before they roll out another frustrating redesign. Design should make life easier. If users have to put in more effort (more scrolling, more searching the screen, tapping through more options) then it’s bad design.

title: Recent update really messed this app up
content:
This app used to be super, literally the best shopping app to use and so easy. Then they “updated it” with completely unnecessary “upgrades”.

The obvious bad malfunction glitches:

2. There’s a solid white blank bar on the bottom blocking a 1/3 of the screen that will not got away no matter what.

The new layout took away the ease of functionality in this app. I imagine the design team thought they were being innovative and updating the look to be more modern, but I liked the old one way better where there were clearly labeled buttons/words that lead you to exactly where you wanted to go. The orders’ page is just an annoying clutter of huge pictures of a few orders. The pictures are of one or two random items from an order, then a huge amount of “keep shopping for” linked pictures on the bottom to desparatelt try to get you to spend more money.

Every page and product page in the app is covered in buy more/similar products pictures. It’s like the hugely misguided advertisers who somehow think putting a ton of commercials during a show will make more people want their product, when it has the exact opposite effect and makes consumers blacklist that brand/item for being so annoying and in-your-face.

It’s like they had no more ideas for improving the old app, because it honestly functioned so well, they tried to make up a bunch of ideas and designs just because there was nothing left to improve. The “update” was so useless and unhelpful, a complete downgrade.

title: Needs improvement
content:
The app works and I haven’t noticed any serious problems (doesn’t crash, can purchase items without glitches and so forth).

I like and use the wish list feature. I’ve got a long list of lists! I’ve found it useful when I’m comparison shopping, and for just saving an interesting item for later.

The things that I really don’t like are:

The app doesn’t have a setting for, or use the system setting, for dark mode.  At this point, the app simply appears terribly outdated because it is not adhering to user interface preference settings like dark mode.

The search function needs help. If I’ve searched for a brand name item, I don’t want to see other similar items from different brands in my results. Having to scroll through so many items is tedious, and I’ve found that even if I use the “filter by brand/type/color” or attempt to make some other specific item feature choice, I still cannot seem to narrow down my search & locate exactly what I’m looking for, unless it has a very unique product name or something. title: More Unnecessary Changes... AGAIN
content:
New feature: the buttons don’t always work.  How many times do YOU have to tap the Add to Cart button before anything actually happens?

Now, search results are HUGE, and navigation buttons have replaced dynamic page length.

An empty cart now has a pointless, irrelevant picture taking up half the screen.

HUGE animated ads are pushing their way into search results, and sponsored results are more obtrusive and annoying than ever.

The advertising engine...I mean, search engine, is practically useless, typically returning a flood of irrelevant results, and the “sorting” function is so poor, it may as well not exist.

To make matters worse, in cases wherein the the “intelligent” parser doesn’t recognize the search terms as “proper” language, it presumes to know the “real” search terms that the user “meant” to enter, and takes it upon itself to change the input, producing a totally irrelevant set of search results.  The user can tap on the search term that was actually entered, producing somewhat more desirable results, BUT if the user attempts to modify the search, the presumed search expression returns magically, messing with the results again.

I have yet to see ANY improvement over the previous version.  In fact, with each successive update, the experience grows increasingly annoying, frustrating, patronizing, insulting, obnoxious and generally unfriendly.

That said, it’s slightly less broken than the web site, on mobile devices.  This is the ONLY reason I’ll bother with it.

It’s a pity the developer doesn’t care one bit about these reviews.

title: Designed for one function—to buy
content:
The app is not designed for users to shop. It is designed for us to buy. All of the work comparing one product to another must be done elsewhere.

I contacted customer service to see if there is a way to select criteria for an item and was told to enter the description into the search window at the top. That method doesn’t allow a buyer to enter more than 3-4 criteria. Many other websites have a much more robust search capability. As the biggest (and richest) online market, I expect more. Buying, not shopping is where Amazon’s efforts are.  In my opinion, the abundant wealth of Amazon’s inventory choices lends itself to shopping for the product that best meets our specific needs, rather than clicking and buying the first thing that pops up.

title: Things that would fix/improve the app...
content:
Things that would fix/improve the app...

1.) “Custom selection” pop-up - dropping to two stars from four because it’s been more than a year and I’ve reported it directly multiple times... but there’s still no fix to the “size selection” bug in “custom selection” pop-ups for items that provide color/size/model choices. The in-app pop-up window for selecting your preference rarely works properly. It WON’T ALLOW YOU TO SCROLL WITH YOUR FINGER. I’ve tried everything from two fingers to swiping in random directions and “zooming out” to “reset” the pop-up. Items that are listed below what’s visible in the box can’t be found and ultimately I’m forced to go to a full browser to make my selection.  This is such a basic function for the world’s largest retailer and yet they won’t even acknowledge the bug. It’s ridiculous that I’m even having to write this down.

PLEASE - for the love of a decent shopping experience - FIX THIS!

2.) Selecting the basket - it would be nice to have a larger (or the option to expand) view of the basket contents relative to the size of an iPad Pro layout. For serious shoppers, sometimes we need to review the content and the pop-up basket size is too small.

3.) UPDATE: FIXED. Fix the search bar “x”. Currently, clicking on the “x” only makes the search history disappear. It’s supposed to clear the entry in the search bar instead so you don’t have to backspace.

4.) UPDATE: FIXED. Fix the wishlist. The last update broke the wishlist “dock” so that clicking on any item in the dock gets you a spinning wheel. The only way to properly access the items is to select the dedicated wishlist page (using the three dots on the dock) and THEN tap on the item you want when the page loads.

5.)UPDATE: FIXED. Provide a place in the app to report bugs.

content:
The mandatory AI search in the Amazon app is awful and makes the shopping experience materially worse. They recently updated every search through an AI layer. This is now slow than a keyword search, produces less predictable results, and gets in the way when I already know exactly what product, brand, model number, or keyword I want to search for.

This is the kind of low-quality “AI slop” that comes from vertically integrated companies forcing their own technology into every part of the customer experience simply because they can, not because it actually improves the product.

Forcing AI into a function that already worked well is not innovation; it is a degradation of the shopping experience.
